Skin MUST be green (olive jade rather than cyan), a very clearly BLACK mohawk crest, black hair only, brown rough peon leather straps with metal buckles, worn short brown trousers and brown boots. Unarmed: empty hands, no gold mace, no axe, no shield, no robe, no cape, no huge armor. Keep the excellent material and muscle shading detail, crisp dark one-pixel contours, lit skin planes and ivory tusks of the reference; DO NOT simplify into flat colored silhouette. Authentic carefully drawn 1990s Game Boy Color RPG sprite artist craftsmanship with modern pixel polish. Six SEPARATE fully isolated sprites on a transparent canvas, with generous empty gutters: four small overworld views across the top (down/front, up/back, left profile, right profile), and two large combat full-body views across the bottom (front three-quarter facing viewer, back three-quarter facing away). The logical overworld sprites are 16x16 and must be interpreted as chunky coarse pixels; the combat front is designed at56x56 logical pixels, and the combat back at48x48, enlarged crisp nearest-neighbor. In combat rear view show rear anatomy and crossed leather straps, not a duplicated frontal face. Left and right must have coherent same silhouette and black crest. Consistent face identity, greens, browns and blacks across all six. Every small mark must be a crisp square pixel cluster; no antialiasing, no soft gradients, no 3D, no ground shadow, no text, no labels, no frames, no background, no grid. All limbs/weapons fit their logical boxes without cropping. Spend detail on the face, tusks, hair silhouette, hands and straps, rather than noisy texture. The user explicitly rejected the previous simplistic procedural sprites: this must look hand-authored, rich and close to their reference.
